node_port.what_it_is: node-port is the capture library's own bare HTTP client: Node's built-in https module (defaultHttpPort, ycharts_session.js:645-669), wired as the 'http' port at :729 and called first by residentClient.get at :329-330. It runs in the same Node process that drives the browser (node ycharts_session.js, run-ycharts-session.sh:55, started by host_capture.py:320), but it is not the browser: the page loads and the sign-in go through the browser's own network stack (Playwright chromium, :1002-1005), while node-port makes one plain GET per call, runs no script, has no redirect handling in the code and solves no challenge. 'node-port' is the label stamped on a reply at :330 and on a failure at :337. Claim measured: read from the code, whose sha256 the order states equals the host's.
node_port.sends: GET only. Headers: User-Agent = the constant UA string (Chrome/148 on Windows, :143-144, the same string the browser context is created with, :154); Cookie = name=value for every cookie returned by context.cookies() at :800 (a one-time snapshot of the browser context's jar, not the live jar; no domain or path filter, :312-313), with the aws-waf-token cookie REMOVED by default (:311-312); Accept 'application/json, text/plain, */*', X-Requested-With 'XMLHttpRequest', Referer = base + '/indices' (:833). The aws-waf-token cookie and an X-AWS-WAF-Token header are added only on the control arm (withWafToken true, :893) and only if the jar holds a token (:314). Node adds Host and Connection by itself, and the code sets no Accept-Language or Accept-Encoding (inferred from the code's silence and from Node's defaults, which are not in the repository). Of the reply it keeps status, body and three headers (location, x-amzn-waf-action, content-type, :658); Set-Cookie is not kept (:655-656), so the jar is never updated by a probe. In the fifth run the jar held 10 cookies with values, 2 of them session names (ycsessionid, csrftoken) and no aws-waf-token, in both arms, so the two arms were the same request (FIFTH_RUN_HOST_SIDE_READ_20261011.md section 2 and ADDENDUM 1 read 6; claim measured on the receipt).

why_the_probe_uses_it.in_words: The code states the reason. At ycharts_session.js:291-297: 'THE RESIDENT'S OWN CLIENT CLASS (CTO word, fourth amendment, 2026-09-24; D1 run 6ade1f06 measured it): the bare Node port carrying the FULL context jar ... On the template route this client read 200 application/json with waf_action null while the in-page fetch read 405 + a captcha action -- the in-page fetch is the class the WAF challenges for a non-navigation request, and it is NOT the class the resident (transport.py headers_for + the stored jar) is.' And at :298-300: 'So the probe's legs go through THIS client first ... no in-page fetch anywhere on the probe path.' And at :824-826: 'the WAF rule is per ROUTE and per CLIENT: the JSON template route admits the Node client with the full jar (run 4: 200 application/json), the HTML route /dashboard/ challenges it (run 5: 405 seven times)'. At :1537-1539 the closing probe 'proves liveness with the tokenless template GET through the resident's client -- the reads the resident makes -- and never reads the page'. The Python side repeats it (generate/recipe.py:373-379). The page is still used for the identity leg (documentIdentity, zero network). Is it deliberately the transport the replay uses? The code states the INTENT: node-port is built to stand in for the resident's client class, and the PRD requires a session to be verified 'from the transport that will use it' (IRPT_BCKEND_PRD.md:51; the mechanism is browserless REST replay, :52). But it is not the same program: the resident is Python urllib (transport.py:468-494), the probe is Node https. They differ in at least the Referer (/dashboard/ in transport.py:477, /indices in :833), in how cookies are chosen (a domain and path matched jar against every cookie in the context) and in the HTTP library that sends them. That the two look the same to the vendor on the wire has no record (absent). The literal replay transport is verified separately after a capture: broker.verify runs step_identity and step_template over the Python transport (session/broker.py:198, :210; host_capture.py:411-412 says so). In the fifth run the Node probe failed first, so that Python verification was never reached. Claim: the stated reasons are measured (quoted from the code); that the two transports are equivalent on the wire is not established.
inferred_parts: that the Node port and the Python urllib client differ on the wire in anything beyond the headers and cookie selection listed (TLS handshake, header order, HTTP/1.1 defaults): inferred from their being two different libraries; no record compares them
that Node adds Host and Connection and no Accept-Language or Accept-Encoding: inferred from Node's defaults and the code's silence

job_calls_after_a_capture.scope: One generation by the resident (generate/resident_worker.py:357-397) plus the session's own check and the sessionless lookup. step_identity (recipe.py:372-390) sends NO request: it grades the identity stored in the bundle. The capture itself (a sign-in by node ycharts_session.js) is the act that gives the job a session, so it is not counted as a call after it.

calls.call: template read GET /custom_pdf_reports/generate/<template id> (the same route the probe reads)
comparison identity read GET /securities/securities_info?securities=... (only when ETF comparisons are requested)
read-back status poll GET /model_portfolios/<id>/status (repeated while calculating)
restart-path reconcile read GET /model_portfolios/fixed/ (the older job path)
the session's own check after a refresh: broker.verify reads the template again (its identity step sends nothing)
PDF download GET of the signed media URL on ycharts-media.s3.amazonaws.com (a different host; no cookie, no credential header)
sessionless ticker lookup GET /securities/securities_info?securities=... (the upload flow's check; no cookie, no session)

job_calls_after_a_capture.how_the_python_calls_are_sent: Every call above except the PDF download and the lookup goes through OperationTransport.request (session/operation_lease.py:242-253), which hands the request to a child Python process (session/deadline_transport.py:26, :59, :110) that builds Transport.from_bundle and calls urllib (generate/transport.py:468-494). The PDF download is the same child in mode 'download' (deadline_transport.py:113-114; resident_worker.py:397). No call after a capture is made by node-port or by the browser. The resident worker runs on the same EC2 host as the capture (journal host ip-172-31-87-2 in IB129-1_journal_capture_attempts.txt), so the two clients leave from the same address (claim measured by the journal; that it is the same egress address to the vendor is inferred).
job_calls_after_a_capture.reason: It cannot be told from code and records. MEASURED on the trunk: (a) the Python path has been answered with the same KIND of reply (a 202 carrying x-amzn-waf-action) before: three research runs on the host stopped WAF_REFRESH_REQUIRED at their 7th call (YCD-R1-20261004T1924Z, YCD-R1-20261004T1944Z, YCD-R3-20261005T0219Z host runs), and the resident journal names READ_BACK_PENDING:WAF_CHALLENGE 14 times on five days, 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-05 (6, 4, 1, 1, 2; IB129-1_journal_capture_attempts.txt lines 59-83); (b) on 2026-10-03T16:35Z the resident runtime read the template route with 200 application/json and no waf action (change_management/20261003T1631Z_irpt-signin-har-20261003_deploy_completion.md, leg V1), on a session seeded from a person's browser. NOT MEASURED: any reply of the Python path to a session captured by the automation after 2026-10-05. No capture has succeeded since, so no job has held such a session; the one Python call the fifth run's job made (17:09:45Z) used the old stored session and was read as SIGNED_OUT, which is a different reply from a challenge (controller.py:40-42 versus :35-37). So whether the post-capture calls of a job would be challenged exactly as the probe was is not told; the first of them (the template read, recipe.py:394) is on the same route as the probe. The journal lines READ_BACK_PENDING:WAF_CHALLENGE show that the Python read path can be challenged on the status route, on days when the stored session was otherwise usable (jobs reached READY on the same days, undivided count), and that the challenge cleared on redelivery. They do not show: a challenge on the template route, on a mutation, or on any day after 2026-10-05; whether the evidence was the header or the body marker (the extract does not say); what the vendor's rule is (the code comments record a firewall window between 122 s and 373 s measured on 2026-10-05, recipe.py comment from 5d3eed8904, resident_worker.py 9e68929699); or anything about a fresh sign-in.
